programme.title: Searching for Sam: Adrian Dunbar on Samuel Beckett
programme.desc: Thirty years after the playwright's death in Paris at the age of 83, Line of Duty star Adrian Dunbar explores the life and work of Samuel Beckett to find out about the man behind Waiting for Godot. Although born and raised in Dublin, Ireland, he was a resident of Paris for most of his adult life, writing in both French and English, and was awarded the 1969 Nobel Prize in Literature for his work

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: Renowned naturalist David Attenborough looks at the evolution of amphibians 350 million years ago, when fish are thought to have crawled from water on to land, spawning newts and salamanders, and he also takes a look at the characteristics of a goliath frog

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Paul Rose visits Ecuador to examine the tale of an 18th-century expedition in which a group of French intellectuals set out to determine the shape of the Earth. The mission was beset by problems from the start as disease, disputes and affairs set the explorers on separate paths and, while great discoveries were made, the team was still to face theft, death and despair

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow's Paul Atterbury recalls the heyday of the great ocean liners, travelling round Britain to reveal a story of design, politics and tragedy as he finds out how these great ships captured the public's imagination. Along the way he uncovers a cinema in Scotland built from the interiors of the SS Homeric, and visits a house in Poole, Dorset, where cabins from the Mauretania have been preserved

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Katie Derham presents from the Royal Albert Hall as the Sinfonia of London performs a programme brimming with colourful orchestration under the baton of their ever-popular artistic director Wilson. The concert opens with Verdi's overture to La Forza del Destino, which is followed by Norwegian cellist Jonathan Aasgaard joining for his Proms solo debut in Walton's Cello Concerto, and finishes with Respighi's Roman Trilogy. Verdi: The Force of Destiny - overture. Walton: Cello Concerto. Respighi: Roman Festivals; Fountains of Rome; Pines of Rome. Jonathan Aasgaard (cello), Sinfonia of London, John Wilson (conductor)

programme.title: Not I
programme.desc: Billie Whitelaw performs Samuel Beckett's dramatic monologue in which the only thing illuminated on stage is the actress's mouth. First broadcast in 1977

programme.title: The Entertainer
programme.desc: Archie Rice is a drunken, lecherous, egotistical vaudevillian whose act is on the downward slope. Adaptation of John Osborne's play, starring Michael Gambon, Billie Whitelaw and Bill Owen. First broadcast in 1993

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: Documentary examining the animals pitting themselves against the world's wildest ocean, unveiling the natural forces that underpin life in the Atlantic. In the vast South Atlantic, huge pods of dolphins, massive penguin colonies and the largest gathering of marine mammals on Earth pack chains of extraordinary islands, created by powerful volcanic forces far below them. Meanwhile, the nutrient-rich upwellings create profusions of life in some areas, and the abyssal depths host a world of bizarre creatures in others

programme.title: A Slow Odyssey
programme.desc: An immersive journey into the world of a green sea turtle, using only natural sounds and embedded graphics to deliver detailed information about its daily routine

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke traces the complex and fascinating story of Western civilisation's love affair with Greek art, learning how people in succeeding centuries found inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Britain, France, Italy and Germany, Alastair visits the Aphrodite of Knidos, which was the first naked woman in Western art; the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice, which became a pawn in an imperial game; and the Discobolus, which was purchased by Nazi leader Adolf Hitler

programme.title: Egypt's Lost Cities
programme.desc: Dallas Campbell and Liz Bonnin join Dr Sarah Parcak on a journey to Egypt to find out whether cities, temples and pyramids are lying beneath the sands. The potential existence of the buildings was suggested by satellites as part of an alternative approach to archaeology

programme.title: Becoming Frida Kahlo
programme.desc: The documentary charts Frida's time in San Francisco with Diego Riera, where her style caused great excitement and she became determined to succeed in her own right. Later, she became shocked by the vast gap between rich and poor that she witnessed in Depression-era New York, and struggled to hide her disdain for high society

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.sub-title: The Secret Life of the Mona Lisa
programme.desc: Alan Yentob tells the story of how Leonardo Da Vinci's Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world. Admired by six million tourists every year, surrounded by bodyguards and encased in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by bullet-proof glass, the enigmatic masterpiece has been stolen, vandalised and exploited over the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, the subject of the portrait is finally revealed - along with the reason behind her inscrutable smile

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.sub-title: Libya - If You Break It You Own It
programme.desc: A look at Barack Obama's first presidential trip abroad to Cairo, where he addressed the younger generation in the Arab world and told them 'you, more than anyone, have the ability to remake this world'. A year and a half later the Arab Spring broke out, leaving Obama to decide whether he should heed the call to save innocent civilians from Muammar Gaddafi's threats of a potential massacre

However, some fish are forced to take their mating rituals away from their territory, putting them at risk from reef mantas - who after feasting, begin their own courtship dances

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Mediterranean Adventure

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: The nation's favourite baking contest has certainly proved it can hold its own after moving to BBC One - this series has been the most entertaining (not to mention contentious) yet. It's about to get a whole lot hotter in the kitchen, though, as it reaches the quarter-final stage, and just five amateur bakers remain. They've all impressed to various extents during Bread Week - at least sufficiently to make it through - but now their skills are thoroughly tested as they take on enriched doughs. They have a signature bake in which they must work with soft dough to create artful works, a technical that sees them recreate an Eastern European cross between bread and pastry, and a showstopper involving doughnuts

programme.title: Life
programme.desc: The focus turns to fish, the most diverse vertebrates on the planet, made up of more than 28,000 species. Off the coast of South Australia, sea dragons pair up for courtship, engaging in a mirror dance before the eggs are laid on the male's tail. Gobies climb up the vertical rocks of Hawaiian waterfalls to access secluded pools at the summit, and flying fish use their elongated pectoral fins to escape from predators. Narrated by David Attenborough

programme.title: Life
programme.desc: The focus turns to birds, revealing the role of their feathers, the ways in which they attract partners and the challenges they face during the nesting season. Narrator David Attenborough provides an insight into the courtship spectacle of the lesser flamingo on Kenya's Lake Bogoria, and follows chinstrap penguins in Antarctica, which make an exhausting climb up a volcano to feed their young

programme.title: Life
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates this series exploring extreme behaviour in the natural world, uncovering some of the strategies animals have developed to stay alive and to breed, from Komodo dragons tackling buffalo to the courtship battle of the humpback whale. He begins by focusing on the methods used by creatures such as cheetahs, bottle-nosed dolphins and Venus fly-traps in their fights for survival

programme.title: Life
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals how reptiles and amphibians, including the pebble toad and Jesus Christ lizard, conquer their shortcomings by using tricks and strategies to avoid predators. He also explores how chameleons can achieve a high level of accuracy with their muscle-propelled, extendible tongues, and finds out how a 9ft-long Komodo dragon can bring down a huge water buffalo

programme.title: World War Weird
programme.desc: Featuring Churchill's plan to create a giant ship out of ice, ghost planes that fly themselves, and a Nazi treasure hunt

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals why male seahorses give birth, and looks at how hyena packs are dominated by the female members

But after 20 years of criss-crossing South America, Jeremy has never seen a specimen big enough to convince him that the fishermen's tales are true.
